newsitem.title: UK: AorTech International makes AIM debut.
newsitem.headline: AorTech International makes AIM debut.

text.p: Shares in mechanical heart valve maker AorTech International Plc made a quiet debut on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) on Wednesday.
By 1330 GMT the shares were quoted at 138-1/2p, setting a premium to their 125p issue price, although no trade was registered in the stock.
The company, based in Scotland, raised 4.5 million stg with the issue, which valued it at 21.5 million stg.
Gordon Wright, executive chairman, said AorTech would use the proceeds to fund marketing and development.
"The monies raised will be used to enhance the marketing of existing products and allow the continuation and expansion of the development programme," Wright said in a statement.
Wright also expressed confidence about AorTech's future prospects.
"We have in place a distribution network, an experienced management team with a proven track record and a range of new products under development which have tremendous potential," he said.
AorTech said it acquired the rights to its core product, the Ultracor tilting disc mechanical heart valve, in 1992.
It is manufactured at Strathclyde Business Park and sold in 18 countries worldwide, mainly through specialist distributors, although the company sells directly to Holland and Germany.

"The response to the Ultracor valve has been very positive and we have achieved excellent market penetration which we can build upon to give sustained growth which will be supplemented by the addition of new products," Wright said.
AorTech also said it had concluded an exclusive worldwide licence agreement for the manufacture and marketing of a new annuloplasty ring used in the repair of damaged heart valves.
